chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba, from Ma'mar ibn Umar ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Kibr (Pride/Arrogance) is the Gown of Allah, and the arrogant one disputes with Allah regarding His Gown.

key_terms.الْكِبْرُ: Pride or arrogance, defined here as a divine attribute
key_terms.الْمُتَكَبِّرُ: The arrogant one, the one who claims superiority
key_terms.رِدَاءُ اللَّهِ: The Gown of Allah, a metaphor for divine majesty and supremacy

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance (kibr) in Shia hadith and its relationship to Allah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from Al-Kafi identifies 'rida' (garment) as a metaphor for divine sovereignty, framing arrogance not merely as a moral flaw but as a theological rebellion where humans usurp Allah's exclusive domain of majesty. This concept is central to the doctrine of Tawhid, illustrating that pride disrupts the proper hierarchical relationship between the Creator and the created by claiming equality with the Divine.
